hook: Light and chromium catalysis couple allylic alcohols with aldehydes to give any of four stereoisomers.
hook_turn: to give any of four stereoisomers.
summary: A chromium catalyst, driven by light, couples allylic and propargylic alcohols with aldehydes to make chiral alcohols, including ones with a quaternary carbon. Choosing the alkene geometry and ligand handedness gives any of the four stereoisomers. Computation explains the stereocontrol, but substrates are lab model compounds.
title: Photomediated Chromium-Catalyzed Regio-, Diastereo-, and Enantioselective Deoxygenative Coupling of Activated Allylic and Propargylic Alcohols with Aldehydes
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
